TIGER SNIP 1.0.2

For installation from the shared drive, double-click Tiger Snip Setup.msi once.
Click Install. Setup confirms success; click Finish to open Tiger Snip with
Launch Tiger Snip checked, or uncheck it to open the app later from the Start menu.
Silent/basic-UI installs, repairs, and removals do not open the app.
No administrator elevation is
required by this installer; your organization's installation policies still apply.
The app is installed locally under %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Tiger Snip.
Personal settings are stored in %LOCALAPPDATA%\Tiger Snip\TigerSnip.ini.
Each Windows user has their own settings. The installer includes no personal settings.
Fresh installations use the new Side panels UI with the Purple light theme.
Existing users keep their saved UI layout and colors.
The standalone Tiger Snip.exe also runs directly and uses those same personal settings.
Windows Installed apps can uninstall Tiger Snip; settings remain for reinstalling.
To reset everything after uninstalling, delete %LOCALAPPDATA%\Tiger Snip.
The welcome screen picks one of ten workplace-friendly headlines each time it opens,
including "The snipping tool of your dreams!" It avoids repeating the last one.

Click New snip, drag an area, and release. Pen is selected automatically.
New captures copy automatically by default. Settings > Auto copy new snips turns this off.
Ctrl+C copies the current image with all annotations, including edits made after capture.
Ctrl+S saves a PNG; Ctrl+Shift+S chooses a new filename.
Ctrl+Alt+F instantly captures all monitors and the mouse pointer, preserving hover menus.
Click Crop in the left tool rail, drag the part to keep, and release.
Esc cancels cropping. Ctrl+Z restores the previous image; Ctrl+Y reapplies the crop.
Annotations move with the crop. Copy and Save export just the cropped image.

Pen: draw with different widths and colors; the cursor previews the brush size and color.
Colors: click + to add a toolbar swatch using the spectrum, RGB, or a hex code.
Right-click any swatch to Edit color or Delete color. Keep four, ten, or more colors;
larger palettes wrap onto extra rows. Your palette and order save on close/exit.
Adding a color selects it; deleting a swatch leaves existing annotations unchanged.
To keep an eyedropper color, click + and Add color. Cancel keeps the palette unchanged.
Highlight: click Highlight, then drag a translucent chisel brush.
It starts yellow at 24 px wide. Color and width (4-80 px) save on close/exit,
separately from Pen. Text stays visible beneath the highlight.
In short windows, tool labels collapse to icons; hover for hints and shortcuts.
Select highlights to move, resize, recolor, or delete them. Undo/redo is supported.
Eraser: click Erase in the left tool rail or choose Edit > Eraser.
Click or drag over a mark to delete the entire drawn stroke or annotation.
Erase an older mark while keeping newer marks elsewhere. At an overlap, a click
removes the topmost annotation. One drag is one undo step; Ctrl+Z restores it.
Esc during a drag cancels that erase. Click Erase again or another tool to leave eraser mode.
The ring cursor shows the contact area. Original screenshot pixels stay intact.
Hold the size + or - button to quickly adjust brush or font size. Move off to pause; release to stop.
Text: click Text in the left tool rail, click the image, and type. Size, Bold, Box, and colors are in the properties panel.
The typing field fits the text and shows the screenshot behind plain text, without an input bar.
Text uses Bahnschrift, a clean modern typeface, with Segoe UI fallback if unavailable.
Enter adds a line. Ctrl+Enter or clicking elsewhere finishes and returns to Select.
Esc cancels. Select Text again to add another annotation; double-click text to edit it again.
Select text to move it. Drag a left/right middle handle to change the wrap width without
changing the font size; widen it to put wrapped text on one line. Top/bottom middle handles
adjust the box height without stretching text, with a minimum that keeps all lines visible.
Corner handles still scale the font. Each resize is one undo step; Esc cancels the drag.
Explicit line breaks stay on separate lines. Text edits support undo/redo.
Eyedropper: click the pipette beside the colors, then click the image.
It samples screenshot/annotation colors and can recolor a selected object. Esc cancels.
Shapes: circles and squares share a menu with large visual style previews.
Choose square, rounded square, highlight box, filled box, or one of the circle styles.
Drag to create; hold Shift for a perfect circle/square. Click Shapes to repeat the last shape; choose rectangles in its style menu.
Use the small arrow beside Shapes, Arrow, Check, and Line to choose a visual style.
Arrows: classic, outlined with a black border, curved gloss, straight gloss, or block gloss.
Block gloss has a wide straight shaft, square tail, triangular head, black border, and highlight.
Line: solid, dashed, or dotted. Hold Shift to snap its angle; click Line in the left tool rail to select it.
Check: choose boxed, circle-badge, or simple green checks and red Xs from its dropdown.
Click to place or drag to size. Switching checks/Xs picks green/red; colors can be customized.
Select: move stickers; drag corners to resize, or arrow/line endpoints to turn.
Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y: undo / redo. Delete removes the selected annotation.
Settings > Toolbar layout switches between Top toolbars and Side panels immediately.
Top toolbars uses the original ribbon and menu bar; Side panels uses the left rail and right properties panel.
The choice and each layout's collapsed controls are remembered separately.
Switching retains your snip, annotations, selection, crop, and undo history.
The controls below describe Side panels; Top toolbars keeps the original controls above the image.
Plain letter keys do not activate tools. Line and Check/X keep their own controls.
The right properties panel follows the current tool or selected annotation.
Its visual style picker retains all circle, rectangle, arrow, check/X and line presets.
Use each tool's small chevron for quick access to its presets.
Choosing a style in the properties panel updates the selected annotation in place.
Stroke and font sizes have preset buttons, a pixel slider, and + / - controls.
Stroke and highlight sliders stop at 40 px for finer control. Use + / - for larger sizes
(up to 100 px for strokes, 80 px for highlights). Font sliders keep their full size range.
A whole slider drag is one undo step.
Esc or loss of pointer capture cancels the drag and restores the previous size.
Opacity adjusts the selected annotation or the next mark, including Copy and Save.
Highlights retain their existing translucent blending beneath the opacity setting.
Undo/redo is beside New snip; Copy and Save are at the top right.
A successful Copy or Ctrl+C brightens the image with a white pulse, fading out in 500 ms.
"Copied to clipboard" stays visible for 1.4 seconds, including on light screenshots.
The pulse follows image transparency and adds no colored tint or outline.
The flash stays in the editor and never appears in copied or saved pixels.
The Settings gear or F10 opens the full settings panel in either UI.
In Top toolbars, Settings > Settings... opens the same panel.
Appearance offers Classic UI (Top toolbars) or New UI (Side panels), three color themes (Purple,
Blue and Teal), and Light or Dark. Colors work with either layout and do not alter exports.
Custom color opens the spectrum, RGB and hex picker for your own UI accent.
Apply color saves it immediately; Cancel keeps the previous theme. The custom color is
remembered when you use another preset. Capture buttons show the exact chosen color in
both layouts and Light/Dark, with readable light or dark text/icons and subtle borders.
Small accent labels and icons adapt for readability.
Top toolbars offers the same picker through Settings > Color theme > Custom color.
General, Capture, Export and View keep every original setting; Actions offers app commands.
Settings save automatically. Esc or Done closes the panel. Scroll shorter panels;
Tab and Enter navigate controls. Top toolbars retains its native menu bar.
Use View to show/hide the command bar, tool rail, or properties panel.
The properties panel's X closes it; its edge chevron reopens it.
The properties panel scrolls when a large palette or short window needs more room.
Chrome visibility is remembered on close/exit. The panel stays hidden without a capture.
Mouse wheel zooms around the pointer, from the fitted minimum up to 800%.
The percentage is actual pixel scale; the fitted minimum adjusts to the window.
Use Select and drag the zoomed image with the hand cursor to pan.
Annotation strokes and handles still move/resize annotations. Middle-drag or
Space+drag also pan. Panning stops at image edges; fitting axes stay centered.
Zooming fully out always centers the complete image. Fit returns to this view.
F11 or View > Full screen opens a full-screen screenshot view.
F11, Esc, or Exit full screen returns to the previous window and toolbar layout.
Full screen retains Recent, Fit and zoom controls in a slim bottom strip.
Each tool remembers its own last color and style, including after File > Exit.
Pen size (1-100 px, shared with shape strokes) is also remembered after restarting.
Highlight width, text size, and each tool's opacity are saved separately.
Text also remembers font size, bold, and the rounded Box setting.
Preferences save on close/exit only. New captures still start with Pen.

Capture in the modern settings panel lets you set two independent global shortcuts.
Top toolbars also offers Settings > Keyboard shortcuts.
Select an area: Ctrl+Alt+S by default, followed by click-and-drag selection.
Instant capture: Ctrl+Alt+F by default, opens all monitors and the pointer in the editor.
Hover a menu and press either shortcut: the screen freezes before focus changes.
Keep the app running for the shortcuts. Backspace disables either one independently.
Single keys work: Print Screen, Page Up, Page Down, F5, Pause or another key.
You can also combine a key with Ctrl, Alt, Shift or Win. Esc cancels recording.
The original shortcut dialog in Top toolbars uses its Save button.
These are global: your assigned key overrides its usual action in other apps.
F12 is reserved. Unavailable shortcuts show an error and keep the previous bindings.
If Print Screen opens Windows Snipping Tool, turn off its Print Screen shortcut in
Windows Settings > Accessibility > Keyboard.
File and the tray menu also offer Capture all monitors now.

General > Software rendering in Side panels switches immediately and saves the choice.
Top toolbars offers Settings > Rendering... to switch how Tiger Snip draws its window.
Check Use software rendering (compatibility mode) if resizing or maximizing
freezes the window, leaves stale content, or takes seconds to redraw.
Leave it unchecked for hardware acceleration, the default for most PCs.
Software rendering may use more CPU on large displays. Click Apply to switch
immediately and save the choice in your personal TigerSnip.ini settings file.
No restart is needed. Copied and saved image quality is unchanged.

Settings > Save location... lets you choose the default folder for saved snips.
Click Use this folder to remember it immediately, including after restarting.
New Save/Save As dialogs start there; you can still choose another destination.
Ctrl+S on an already saved snip updates its existing file.

Settings > Professional Border > Enabled is optional and OFF by default.
Blur and Rounded corners show OFF and are unavailable until Professional Border is on.
Turning it on restores your saved choices (both effects are selected initially).
Uncheck either in the submenu to use the other alone.
It adds a soft gray halo without a hard outline and/or rounded corners to Copy and PNG Save.
Blur adds 20 px transparent padding per side (40 px more in width/height).
Rounded corners alone keep the original dimensions.
The screenshot content stays at its original size without tinting or fading.
The individual settings are remembered on close/exit and appear immediately in the image preview.

Settings > Samtec Logo is optional and OFF by default.
Its submenu shows six choices: White badge and Soft watermark for the S, tiger, and wordmark.
Selecting a style enables it; uncheck Enabled to turn it off and keep that style.
White badges have compact rounded backgrounds and soft gray halos.
Soft watermarks are faint monochrome marks without a card or orange underline.
They adapt to light/dark backgrounds; a subtle edge halo keeps the artwork visible.
All logos are smaller, with the watermarks more compact than the white badges.
The bottom-right logo scales with the snip and works with or without Professional Border.
Small snips keep a recognizable minimum logo size; very tiny or narrow snips limit its footprint.
Enabled and selected style are remembered on close/exit; the preview shows/hides the logo immediately.

Recent keeps the last 10 captures, including the current one, in this PC's memory.
Click Recent or press Ctrl+Shift+R to reopen a capture with its editable annotations.
Right-click a recent thumbnail and choose Copy to copy it directly with its annotations
and current export effects, keeping your current snip open. The welcome capture icon
also starts a new snip when clicked.
Closing the window leaves Tiger Snip in the tray and retains those captures.
Closing, exiting, and taking a new snip happen immediately without a save prompt.
Click the tray icon to snip. File > Exit quits entirely and clears the capture collection.
Captures are not saved as projects or restored after restarting.
Settings > Run at sign-in is optional and disabled by default.

Settings save in your Windows user profile; the shared release folder can be read-only.
Keep the accompanying runtime notices if sharing the standalone EXE.
If Run at sign-in is enabled, disable it before uninstalling the app.

The preview shows the same logo, blur, rounded corners, and padding as Copy and PNG Save.

DATA HANDLING
Tiger Snip has no application networking or telemetry. Recent captures, original crop
pixels, and undo history stay in local process memory until Exit or oldest eviction.
Copy places an image on the Windows clipboard, where it can remain after Tiger Snip exits.
Windows clipboard history/synchronization and other apps are controlled separately.
Save writes a PNG wherever you choose, including a network or synchronized folder.
An interrupted save can leave an adjacent temporary or recovery image file.
Eraser removes annotations; it does not erase the underlying screenshot. Highlight
is translucent. Cropping is reversible in Recent/undo while the app is running.

SUPPORT
Maintainer/problem reports: Jack Kempf, jack.kempf@samtec.com.

SAVING AND RECOVERY FILES
Each save uses a unique temporary filename. Forced termination can leave an
adjacent .tiger-snip-{GUID}.tmp or .tmp.previous recovery file containing image
data. It will not block later saves. Old leftovers are not automatically deleted;
ask Jack/IT to inspect recovery needs before removing a specifically identified file.

UPDATING THIS SAME 1.0.2 PACKAGE
Close Tiger Snip and disable Run at sign-in if enabled. Uninstall the previous
copy using Windows Installed apps, then install the replacement MSI. Preferences
survive. Do not bypass company installation/security policy to force a repair.
